speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help identify the cause of your bleeding, can you tell me if you have a personal or family history of bleeding disorders, and have you noticed any other symptoms like frequent nosebleeds or heavy menstrual periods?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient was brought in by his mother for persistent bleeding following elective removal of wisdom teeth. The bleeding from the surrounding gums was minimally responsive to multiple gauze packs. The patient also has a history of easy bruising. Family history includes the patient's uncle who had similar issues with bleeding and a history of easy bruising and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: The family history of joint swelling and easy bruising in your uncle strongly suggests a clotting factor deficiency. I need to check your coagulation profile to confirm this, so REQUEST TEST: aPTT.

speaker: Doctor
text: Your prolonged aPTT supports a suspicion of Hemophilia A or B, given the family history of joint swelling. To distinguish between the two, I need to check the specific factor levels, so REQUEST TEST: Factor_VIII_Level.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since your Factor VIII levels are normal, we can rule out Hemophilia A. Given the family history of joint bleeding and the prolonged aPTT, I suspect Hemophilia B, so I will check your Factor IX levels. REQUEST TEST: Factor_IX_Level

speaker: Doctor
text: Normal Factor IX levels rule out Hemophilia B, so we must consider other causes of a prolonged aPTT like Von Willebrand Disease or Factor XI deficiency. REQUEST TEST: Von_Willebrand_Factor_Assay

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal vWF, Factor VIII, and Factor IX levels, but a prolonged aPTT and a family history of bleeding with joint issues, Factor XI deficiency is the most likely diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Factor_XI_Level

speaker: Doctor
text: The low Factor XI level confirms the diagnosis, especially given the prolonged aPTT and family history of bleeding. DIAGNOSIS READY: Factor XI Deficiency
